By far one of the most pointless courses in this department. I learned nothing, didn’t gain any valid experience, and was only left with my wasted time and effort. There are only three projects throughout the semester, but to be honest, it’s hard to decipher which one is the absolute worst. I’m not handsy with cameras, and I would be able to take up the full blame if the department did its best to teach me, which didn’t happen. Even in the first semester, I never got to experiment with a camera, as thoroughly as I needed to feel adequate. And this semester, we were left to work with professionals, outside people. With the insufficient time given for projects that, in my opinion, either require a longer period or more people to work, it was unfair to expect a professional final product. I don’t understand how the department can be oblivious to the time we spent online and feel okay with suddenly making us work with actual clients. For people who possess interest in filmmaking and a passion for the camera, I guess this studio can be useful and you can maybe have fun with it, but that doesn’t mean the syllabus makes any sense. I didn’t have this sort of passion to begin with, and this course made my dislike turn into hatred. I find it irrational to force all students into such extensive projects concerning only filmmaking or videography because COMD isn’t solely structured on these two areas. Why am I being forced to put immense effort and huge blocks of time into projects that won’t serve any purpose for my career? This would be okay if it was the 1st or 2nd year studio, but I as a 3rd year student feel like my time shouldn’t be wasted because of a fruitless syllabus structure. This studio would be great if it was one of the electives, and would definite make more sense. Mandatory studio courses should be flexible and people in their last 2 years should be able to pick the medium they want to work with. This department isn’t advertised or labeled as “film only”.
